solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Glaze a special ice cream for starters

indicators.note: for starters asks for the opening letter of each of the words that come before it

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for special, as in S for a special edition

explanation.surface: A dessert recipe: put a glaze on a special ice cream before the meal begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for starters' takes the first letter of each word: A, the S from 'special', and the I and C of 'ice cream'. 'special' gives S, then S again as its own first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly used as a shiny coating on cold dishes, so it is a kind of glaze.

clue.text: See 23
Punishing repayment loan; contents lost forever

indicators.note: punishing suggests rough treatment, so the letters that follow are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: contents lost says the inside of the next word drops out, leaving just its two ends

explanation.surface: A harsh loan repayment that has swallowed the borrower's money for good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents lost' leaves LN from 'loan'; 'Punishing' shuffles REPAYMENT plus LN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done permanently lasts for all time, which is what forever means.

clue.text: Held up in Tunisia, lacking port

indicators.note: Held up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone stranded in Tunisia without a harbour to sail from.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Held up' means read upwards, so SIALAC, found across 'Tunisia, lacking', is read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Calais is the French ferry port facing Dover across the Channel.

clue.text: Ex-PM flying to JFK second last in economy, going for a pound

indicators.note: second says it is the second instance of that letter in the phrase that is swapped
going for means one letter departs and another takes its place

parts.note: flying to JFK airport is going to New York by air: TO NY BY AIR

indicators.note: last in points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: L, from the Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A former prime minister flies economy class to New York.
explanation.walkthrough: In TO NY BY AIR, the second Y (Y being the last letter of 'economy') is swapped for L, giving TO NY BL AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Blair was Labour prime minister of the UK from 1997 to 2007, so he is a former PM.

clue.text: Where bride drops her underwear in 3?

definitions.text: Where bride drops her underwear in 3?

parts.words: Where bride drops her underwear in 3?
parts.note: a bride's collection of linen and lingerie for married life is gathered under a French name, 3 being Calais in France

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a honeymooning bride undressing in a French port.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is French, which is why the clue points at Calais (3). The blogger found the clue tenuous.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride collects for her marriage, including her underwear, and the word comes from French.

clue.text: Top of the charts is Adele's latest cacophony

parts.note: the top of the charts is number one, written NO 1, with the figure read as the letter I
is shortens to 's, as in it's

indicators.note: latest asks for the final letter of the singer's name

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that the chart-topping new Adele single is just a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'latest' takes the E from 'Adele's'; ADELE is the British pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cacophony is a harsh, discordant din, which is what noise is.

clue.text: Defence of a ruck developing under Boris's leadership

indicators.note: under in a down answer places the following piece below the first
leadership asks for the leading, first letter of the name
developing suggests something changing form, so the letters rearrange

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugby scrum forming under Boris Johnson's command, standing for his political defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges OF A RUCK into ACKFOUR, set under the B that 'leadership' takes from 'Boris's'. A ruck is a loose scrum in rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: In football the back four are the four defenders across the back line, so they form a team's defence.

clue.text: A number left outskirts of Egyptian capital

indicators.note: left outskirts of means the city's edges are left behind, taking away its first and last letters

parts.note: Cairo is the capital city of Egypt

explanation.surface: A count of people who left the edge of Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number' looks like the start of the wordplay, but it is the definition: a number is a song.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune, and a number is a song or piece of music in a performance.

clue.text: Pink paper takes 24hrs; that's fast!

parts.note: rose is a pink colour
the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
twenty-four hours make a day

explanation.surface: The pink Financial Times takes a whole day to read; how fast is that?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pink paper' suggests the FT but splits into colour and newspaper. THE SUN is a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose Sunday is a Sunday in Lent, the Christian season of fasting, hence the exclamation about fasting.

clue.text: Endless gutrot claims sick Montmartre painter

indicators.note: claims means takes in, so one piece holds the other inside it
endless says the word loses both its ends, leaving only the inner letters

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Cheap booze takes its toll on a bohemian painter in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' leaves UTRO from 'gutrot', which 'claims' ILL. Gutrot is British slang for cheap, rough alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Utrillo was a French painter famous for his street scenes of the Montmartre district of Paris.

clue.text: Leading Brexiteer "entertaining comedian" — papers

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: IDS is Iain Duncan Smith, a leading campaigner for the UK to leave the EU
a card is a joker or funny person

explanation.surface: A newspaper report on a Brexit campaigner hosting a stand-up comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading Brexiteer' tempts you towards Johnson or Farage; the initials of Iain Duncan Smith, a prominent Leave campaigner, are what fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Identity cards are official documents, and papers is a common word for such documents.

clue.text: EU "falsities" so besmirched much of the campaign rhetoric

indicators.note: besmirched means dirtied or smeared, so the letters are messed up into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that EU falsehoods smeared the Brexit referendum campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'besmirched' rearranges EU FALSITIES SO.
explanation.definitionFit: A tissue of lies is a web of untruths, a jaundiced view of political speeches during the referendum.

clue.text: I support Hibernian; I must be barking

indicators.note: support in a down answer means the piece stands below the other, holding it up

parts.note: Hibernian means from Ireland, Hibernia being its Latin name
the compiler of a crossword calls themselves the setter

explanation.surface: A football fan says they back Hibernian, the Edinburgh club, and admits they must be mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Hibernian is also a Scottish football club; here it simply means Irish. 'barking' looks like British slang for mad but the dog barks.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of red gun dog barks, so it could say of itself that it must be barking.

clue.text: Self-catering rooms vacant, water included, for hacks

indicators.note: included says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: SC is the usual abbreviation for self-catering in holiday listings

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word remain

parts.note: the Ribble is a river in northern England

explanation.surface: Holiday lets with empty rooms and running water, advertised to journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' is a river here: the Ribble flows through Lancashire in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Hacks are writers of low quality, especially journalists, and scribblers is a disparaging word for them.

clue.text: Key section of Article 50

indicators.note: section of says only a part of the words that follow is wanted, here the tail of the first word running into the next

parts.note: the number is read in words as fifty, and its opening letter carries the run on

explanation.surface: The key part of Article 50, the EU treaty clause for a country leaving the union.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 50 in words: the answer is a section running across 'artiCLE Fifty'. The parse keeps the tail of 'Article' and the F opening 'fifty' because the figure is printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the sign on a music staff that sets the pitch, and in music it is called a key.

clue.text: Old forerunner of the Euro made Toni a killing

parts.note: ex means former or old
the ECU, the European Currency Unit, came before the euro

indicators.note: made means formed or built, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone named Toni made a fortune trading in the old European currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges TONI into TION. 'a killing' looks like a big profit, but it is a death.
explanation.definitionFit: An execution is the putting to death of someone, which is a killing.

clue.text: At home, relatively speaking, in 3

definitions.meaning: at home means informally, among one's own household
among relatives, put into the language of Calais (3), that is in French

explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively speaking' looks like a stock phrase meaning comparatively, but it means speaking of relatives. 3 is CALAIS, so 'in 3' means in French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means within the family, so it describes being at home with one's relatives.

clue.text: Try Thai-sounding recipe that's more wholesome

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it

indicators.note: sounding says the word before is to be taken by its pronunciation rather than its spelling

parts.note: Thai, from Thailand, is pronounced like tie
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A tip to try a recipe that sounds Thai because it is healthier.
explanation.walkthrough: HEAR plus a word pronounced like 'Thai' plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty food is nourishing and filling, so a heartier dish is more wholesome.

clue.text: Has nothing on international hard drug expert

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a buff is an enthusiast or expert

explanation.surface: A report on an international expert on hard drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has nothing on' looks like a comparison (is no better than) but means is naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be naked is to be wearing nothing at all, which is what this informal phrase means.

clue.text: Easy Rider's direction?

parts.note: a horseman's call telling his mount to steady up and slow down; easy is what riders say to calm a horse

explanation.walkthrough: 'Easy Rider' looks like the 1969 biker film and its director, but a rider says 'easy' to a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the command a horse rider calls out to make the animal stop or slow down.

clue.text: Dry American who helped to finish me off?

definitions.text: who helped to finish me off?

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

explanation.surface: Julius Caesar asks which dry-witted American helped kill him.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Julius, so 'me' is Julius Caesar.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutus was one of the conspirators who stabbed Julius Caesar to death.

clue.text: Regret at having made investment purchase; error seems careless

parts.note: to purchase is to buy

indicators.note: careless suggests sloppiness, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shopper regrets an investment that, through careless error, went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'careless' rearranges ERROR SEEMS, after BUY.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom names the regret people feel after a purchase they think was a mistake.

clue.text: How some cure habit?

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asks by what means certain people beat an addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' looks like 'some people' but it signals the hidden letters in 'cuRE HABit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehabilitation, in the form of a clinic course, is the way addicts are treated, so it answers the question how.

clue.text: Retiree, inviting Liberal Democrat out for drink, is mugged

indicators.note: out for suggests going round, so the drink is wrapped around the rest

parts.note: to sup is to drink

indicators.note: inviting means taking in a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: OAP stands for old-age pensioner
LD is short for Liberal Democrat, a British political party

explanation.surface: A pensioner takes a Lib Dem out for a drink and gets robbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is mugged' looks like street robbery, but the phrase means conned. The blogger was unsure how 'out for' signals the drink going round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sold a pup is to be swindled with something worthless, and mugged is slang for being conned.

clue.text: People determined to leave his glen ravaged?

indicators.note: ravaged means devastated, so the letters are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish laird leaves the valley that was wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ravaged' rearranges HIS GLEN. 'People determined to leave' refers to the Brexit vote; England voted to leave the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: The voters of England backed leaving the European Union in 2016, so the nation was determined to leave.

clue.text: Leading Brexiteer "pointless, common politician"

indicators.note: pointless means losing a compass point, here east

parts.note: Michael Gove was a leading campaigner for leaving the EU

explanation.surface: A sneer that a leading Brexit campaigner is a pointless, vulgar politician.
explanation.walkthrough: E (east) is a compass point, so 'pointless' takes E from GOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gov is a casual short form for governor, an elected leader in US states, so an informal word for a politician.

clue.text: Nigel, losing his head, over-the- top, barking? Time to move on

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters go wild into a new order
losing his head means the name gives up its first letter

parts.note: OTT is the usual short form of over-the-top

explanation.surface: Nigel Farage, gone mad and excessive, should step aside.
explanation.walkthrough: IGEL and OTT are rearranged by 'barking' (British slang for mad).
explanation.definitionFit: To let something go is to stop dwelling on it and move on.

clue.text: Half-hearted crowd follows famous golfer, vulnerable to the cut?

indicators.note: follows places the crowd after the golfer

parts.note: Seve Ballesteros was a celebrated Spanish golfer

indicators.note: half-hearted means half of the double letter at the centre is dropped

parts.note: a rabble is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A lukewarm crowd trails a star golfer who might miss the cut.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBLE loses one of its central Bs. 'the cut' is golf's halfway elimination, but here it means separation.
explanation.definitionFit: Something severable can be cut off or separated, so it is open to being cut.

clue.text: Dashes back to get precious instrument

indicators.note: back says the word is to be read from right to left

parts.note: darts are quick rushes, as dashes are

explanation.surface: Someone rushes back to fetch a valuable violin.
explanation.walkthrough: DARTS read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strad is a Stradivarius violin, among the most valuable instruments in the world.
